programme.title: The World of Biblical Israel
programme.sub-title: Biblical Israel - The Story of a People
programme.desc: Entering the world of biblical Israel with a historical overview; an examination of how the Bible gives insights into the daily life of ancient Israelites; considering the context for how the Bible comes into being.

programme.title: The World of Biblical Israel
programme.sub-title: By the Rivers of Babylon - Exile
programme.desc: A look at the Babylonian exile; the exiled Judeans begin asking themselves who they are as a people and why they are conquered; as the Bible begins to be compiled in this time of exile, it offers two vantage points for understanding its history.

programme.title: The World of Biblical Israel
programme.desc: Surveying the stories of ancient Israel's origins as preserved in the book of Genesis; these origin stories are crucial for understanding the books that follow because ancient Israel understands itself to be a family that descends from Jacob.

programme.title: The World of Biblical Israel
programme.desc: A look at Moses; the story of the Israelites' exodus from Egypt; tracing the narrative of Moses's journey, which includes receiving the Ten Commandments from Yahweh; reviewing the Torah, the "law of Moses"; the origins of the priesthood.

programme.title: Herodotus: The Father of History
programme.desc: Identifying key issues of definition and terminology; explaining what is known about the life of Herodotus; background on the ancient Greek world; summarizing the momentous events, particularly the Persian Wars, that spur Herodotus to write.

programme.title: Herodotus: The Father of History
programme.desc: Herodotus is not the first Greek to write about the past; knowing makes him original; how he explains, in the very first sentence of his work and one that richly rewards close reading, the what, why and how of his monumental effort.

programme.title: Herodotus: The Father of History
programme.desc: Knowing how Herodotus deals with the vast and complicated body of traditional narratives that inform the Greek world; how his subject matter and his angle on it both resemble and differ from older accounts of the ways and causes of things.

programme.title: Herodotus: The Father of History
programme.sub-title: Homeric Epic and the East-West Conflict
programme.desc: For all ancient Greeks, Homer is a pervasive influence; how Herodotus models his work on the "Iliad" and the "Odyssey"; how and why does he depart from the Homeric and give the uniquely Herodotean.

programme.title: Classical Mythology
programme.desc: Setting the stage by defining key terms; outlining some problems that develop when studying classical mythology; including synopses of specific myths; discussions of their cultural background; examinations of larger issues implied by them.

programme.title: Classical Mythology
programme.desc: What the most influential theorists say about the origin, nature and function of myth; what distinguishes myth from legend and folklore; whether myth can be understood as a subcategory of something else; whether it plays some universal psychic role.

programme.title: Classical Mythology
programme.desc: Continuing the examination of ideas about myth; psychological theories of Sigmund Freud and Carl Jung; structuralist approaches of Claude Levi-Strauss and others; the work of Joseph Campbell, a psychological and metaphysical theorist of myth.

programme.title: Classical Mythology
programme.desc: In his "Theogony", the Greek poet Hesiod describes the creation of the universe through the creation of the gods; how Hesiod's version of the creation story compares with the much later Roman version preserved in Ovid's "Metamorphoses".

programme.title: The Other Side of History: Daily Life in the Ancient World
programme.sub-title: Taking On the Other Side of History
programme.desc: The past comes alive when considering the imaginary lives of ordinary people; these include the citizens, soldiers and slaves who live on the other side of history; asking questions that many textbooks never ask.

programme.title: The Other Side of History: Daily Life in the Ancient World
programme.desc: Taking a look at the lives of human ancestors; picturing oneself as a Neanderthal, whose life is dominated by the environment; discovering the significance of the human mind, language and art in the Old Stone Age.

programme.title: The Other Side of History: Daily Life in the Ancient World
programme.desc: Stepping into the world's earliest permanent settlement; why the development of agriculture is a revolution; the invention of writing; the creation of laws; an increase in trade; technological innovations such as the wheel.

programme.title: The Other Side of History: Daily Life in the Ancient World
programme.desc: What it is like to be an ancient Egyptian; exploring everyday life during the New Kingdom era; the richness of the Nile; the conservatism and stability of the society; relics that survive across millennia, such as hieroglyphics, papyri and art.

programme.title: The World of Biblical Israel
